---
id: P-glance-disclosure-01
form: pattern
claim: "For a glanceable overview: put what users often need on the first screen and the rest one step down (corroborated: Nielsen 2006 'You have to disclose everything that users frequently need up front, so that they have to progress to the secondary display only on rare occasions'; Apple Widgets 'Create a layout that provides essential information at a glance and allows people to view additional details by taking a longer look'). A tap should open the matching detail directly (Apple Widgets, Live Activities). A glance surface need not show everything; prioritise the most useful (Apple Live Activities). A one-line text summary or small preview chart helps (Apple Charting data). Label the link so it sets clear expectations for the next level (Nielsen only; Budiu's information-scent page covers link-label accuracy, not the same claim, so not corroborated). Keep to at most two disclosure levels (Nielsen only, single source). Not documented: what belongs on a phone's first screen for several projects, item counts, a time budget for a glance, gauges."
grade: B
topics: [design, dashboards, mobile]
checked_on: 2026-10-08
shelf_life: 24 months
opened_by: source-checker (Q-013, 2026-10-08); NN/g HTML and Apple JSON through a summarising fetch, not raw
memo: research/Q-013-memo.md
publisher_note: grade B because the two-level limit and label advice are single source; the first-screen principle alone is corroborated by different authors
sources:
  - https://www.nngroup.com/articles/progressive-disclosure/
  - https://www.nngroup.com/articles/information-scent/
  - https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/widgets
  - https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/live-activities
  - https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/charting-data
---
---
id: P-stale-visible-01
form: pattern
claim: "Apple Widgets: if people may check more often than the data updates, show text saying when it was last updated, and show content quickly without hiding stale data behind placeholder content. Apple Live Activities: if the underlying status is unchanged, keep the same display. NN/g (Kaplan 2021): state plainly when there is no data; 'Inaccurate system-status messages for empty states are particularly harmful.' Tension: Apple Loading says to show placeholders while content loads and to say clearly that it is loading; Apple gives both for different contexts and neither is chosen here. Not documented: making stale data visibly fade or degrade; unknown values in a gauge or number tile."
grade: B
topics: [design, dashboards]

## 6. Value and stop rule
*This project's own measure of value, the target and date, and what counts as a miss — including the cost to the owner's time. Write each value target on its own line starting with its ID, like `V1: <measure>, <target>, <date>`; spec criteria trace to these IDs.*

*Proposed values; the owner sets them on the move-to-Build card.*

V1: Missed decisions: items waiting on the owner in a connected project that the desk did not show within 5 minutes, 0 over the first 14 days after launch, 2026-11-25 (14 days after V4's date; moves with it)
V2: False alarms: items the desk flagged that did not need the owner, at most 1 a week over the first 14 days after launch, 2026-11-25 (14 days after V4's date; moves with it)
V3: Owner upkeep: the owner's time on the desk itself (tokens, settings, adding repositories), at most 30 minutes a week after launch, 2026-11-25 (14 days after V4's date; moves with it)
V4: Replacement: the desk serves the Operations-Hub address and the old repository is archived, by 2026-11-11
V5: Owner response time: the median time from a card appearing in a connected project to its answer being committed, counting only 07:00 to 22:00 Monday to Friday (America/Chicago), with a card still open at the window's end counted at its wait so far, tracked and shown on the desk, under 4 hours, over the first 14 days after launch, 2026-11-25 (14 days after V4's date; moves with it)

V4's date is proposed as 2026-11-11, the Chief of Staff's estimate with D7 (E: about two weeks for a model change's spec, build, review and owner approval, then
its adoption here). The owner sets the date on the
move-to-Build card. V1 to V3 run for the 14 days after launch, so their date is V4's date plus 14

  rule, its untracked ones folded into one "not tracked" line a tap opens;

- **The milestone** (for the owner, below). No line in docs/PROJECT.md section 3 covers this work;
  M3D is reached (2026-10-24). Each ruling's record says "Milestone: none (a design follow-up after
  M3D; the planner gives it a milestone when it is built)". So this plan proposes one, as M3D's was
  made: a Build-phase line the Chief of Staff drafts, the Critic checks and the owner approves,

  (M3E) · done when each phase on a project's page counts all its milestones and sprints, the
  standard checklist sits in its own group, finished and failed marks are green and red, a small
  arrow marks where each project is now, and a page's most important things sit in a soft box, each

- **Open for the owner** (under "Open questions for the owner", "Open: after the glance audit's

input.content:
**After the glance audit, round 2** (added 2026-11-03, "After the glance audit's round 2: your five
answers and the hierarchy of work"; draft 1)
*From the owner's five rulings (decisions/questions/P-001-glance2-anchor.md, -arrow.md, -counts.md,
-palette.md and -standard.md), the owner's go-ahead for the hierarchy of work
(docs/design/references/owner-request-2026-10-24-glance-emphasis.md), and the Design reviewer's
proposals they accept (docs/design/audit-2026-10-24-round-2.md, items 1 to 5, "the audit"). The desk
is mockup v2 as built (AC44), with the round-1 choices as their baseline (the amendment, "Builds on
round 1"). Each criterion names the criteria it changes; where they differ, it governs. Every
screen keeps AC81's tokens and AC88's dark theme, and every mark keeps its shape and its word, so
colour is never the only carrier of meaning (AC42; WCAG 1.4.1, library/facts/F-wcag22-01.md).*

- AC91 [trace: V1 → AC91] [trace: V4 → AC91] — When the owner opens a screen, then the few things
  that matter most on it, and only those, sit in a soft box in the look of Home's briefing, so the
  eye lands there first; such boxes stay occasional, and on the desk's screens a filled box means
  nothing else.
  - The ruling: P-001-glance2-anchor.md, line 1 (quoted in the amendment). The owner's words: "the
    outlined box isn't ONLY for the single most important thing on the page. It should be for the
    set of most important things on a page. It definitely shouldn't be overdone but only accepting
    one thing omits other elements that might be close to or as important." The option as put: "The
    project page gets the boxed sentence and tally; the rule holds desk-wide; the why-not-written box
    becomes a plain line." The owner's round-2 ask: "the occasional usage of outlined boxes or subtle
    callouts that an assist as visual anchors on pages for the most important information on it".
  - **The form** (the audit, item 2, "one form"): Home's briefing's own look: the `--bg2` ground,
    radius 12 px, padding 12 px, a 6 px gap between its lines, text in `--ink` in the roles the
    lines already have. No edge of any kind: no border, no outline, no edge in `--line`, `--line2`
    or vermilion (an edged thing on the desk is one to tap or type into, and `--bg2` with a
    `--line2` edge is the text box's look). Its ground is never vermilion. A mark inside it keeps
    its own colour (the briefing's ◆ stays vermilion).
  - **What may sit in one** (the widened rule): the set of a screen's most important things, such as
    where a project stands, what needs the owner and how far the work has come. One box may hold
    several of them. Never a gap the agents fill (AC69), never inside a card, tile, sheet or bubble,
    and never used for decoration.
  - **Never overdone** (C, the reading of "It definitely shouldn't be overdone"; put to the owner,
    "Open: after the glance audit's round 2"): at most two anchors on any screen, holding at most six
    lines between them at 360 px wide; a screen may have none.
  - **Where, as ruled:**
    - **Home:** the briefing (AC82), unchanged; it is the anchor that sets the look;
    - **a v3 project's page:** AC83's one sentence and, under it, one tally line, in one box at the
      top of the Overview, where the sentence sits today: the tally is AC94's head, "<R> of <T>
      milestones reached · <the sprints part>" (as drawn by the audit, "8 of 16 milestones reached ·
      17 sprints: 9 merged, 8 not read"); from stage 6 it adds " · <d> of <t> pieces done" where AC96
      gives it. The strip and the ◆ row stay outside it (the audit's reasons: the box's padding broke
      "Discovery" mid-word at 360 px, and the ◆ row is anchored by vermilion and is absent when
      nothing waits);
    - **a v2.5 project's page:** its sentence alone (AC83, frame 8), with no tally, since it has no
      milestones (C);
    - **every other screen** (the Timeline, Plan, Waiting, the sheets, Team and its member pages,
      Details, the portfolio's block and the failed-load page): none, as the audit's table has them,
      until the Design reviewer's per-screen table names one;
    - **a further anchor** (the widened rule) only where the Design reviewer's per-screen table in a
      stage's build brief names it, with what it holds and why it is among the screen's most
      important things, within the bound above; the Reviewer checks it against this criterion. Item
      4c, Waiting's Done lane shaded on `--bg2` (the owner's comment, the owner-request record's
      "Comment on item 4b"), is settled in that table with the lanes ruling (P-001-glance-lanes.md,
      C), and built with it.
  - **What stops being a box:** the why-once line on an opened phase ("Why each is taken on or
    skipped: not written yet. <project>'s Chief of Staff writes its lines.", AC83 and AC90) becomes
    a plain line in `--t-small`, in the agents' grey with its eye icon, on the list's own ground; its
    words are unchanged (AC83, AC90; P-001-why-line.md's words stand).
  - **Kept as built** (C): the Timeline's two end cards ("What we're delivering" and "Where we
    started", AC59) and Plan's card. They are not at the top of their screens, and the audit's
    table keeps them; the Design reviewer's table may list them as that screen's anchors or as cards.
  - A test marked `ac-test: S-001/AC91` renders every trial-view screen from each fixture
    (`service-desk/`, `poom/`, `md-extremes/`) and made-up cases (labelled NOT real) in light and dark,
    and checks, reading the CSS as AC88's cascade does: the anchor rule's ground, radius, padding and
    gap, and that it has no `border`, `outline` or `box-shadow` and no `--you` ground; at most two
    anchors on each screen, holding at most six lines at 360 px, each in a place this criterion or
    the stage's table names, and none inside a card, tile, sheet or bubble; the project page's box
    holding its sentence and tally (a v2.5 page its sentence only); the why-once line with no ground
    of its own, its words unchanged; and Home's briefing unchanged. The stage's pull request carries
    Chromium captures of the project page at 360 × 740 and 414 × 896, light and dark, with nothing
    scrolling sideways and "Discovery" whole on the strip.

- AC92 [trace: V4 → AC92] — When the owner looks at a drawing of where a project is, on the
  Timeline, a project page's phase strip, a Home tile, Plan or an opened phase, then one small
  filled triangle in ink points at the present, and nothing else on the desk uses that shape.
  - The ruling: P-001-glance2-arrow.md, line 1. The option as put: "The triangle on all five
    drawings; the ▲ reading arrow removed." The owner's ask: "On any timeline element or plan
    element, can we are add a subtle but noticeable visual arrow indicator for where we are?"
  - **The shape** (the audit, item 3): a filled triangle in `--ink`, pointing at the present: right
    on a drawing read down the screen, down on one read across it, never up. It is drawn as a shape
    (a CSS `clip-path` polygon or an inline SVG in `currentColor`), never a text character, so it
    looks the same on every phone (AC81's rule for marks). It is hidden from assistive technology
    (`aria-hidden`): the words beside it already say now, Now or next to reach. It never animates,
    and moves only when its drawing does. Ink stands at 17.58:1 (light) and 16.25:1 (dark) on `--bg`
    and 16.99:1 and 15.15:1 on `--card` (the audit, measured), above WCAG 1.4.11's 3:1.
  - **Where, one per drawing, in the audit's sizes:**
    - **the Timeline** (AC84): at the Now line, an 8 × 10 px triangle pointing right, centred on the
      rail, in place of the line's 16 × 2 px bar; one per Timeline;
    - **a project page's strip** (AC83): a 10 × 6 px triangle pointing down, centred above the now
      cell's bar, in the gap between the anchor (AC91) and the strip;
    - **a Home tile** (AC82): a 6 × 8 px triangle pointing right, 3 px left of the now run's now
      cell;
    - **Plan** (AC86): a 6 × 8 px triangle pointing right, in the page's 16 px margin beside the row
      whose icon is the gold ring (next to reach, AC57's state), one per project group. A gate card's
      row at the group's top takes none (it is not a milestone, AC86's note);
    - **an opened phase** (AC83): a 6 × 8 px triangle on the phase's thin line, beside its
      next-to-reach row, in the now phase only.
  - **Where there is no present** (C): no triangle where AC50 gives no now (its "not recorded", and
    a tile or page that says "not available", "Checking…" or "Can't read"), nor on Plan in a group
    with no next-to-reach row. A Done project: on its tile the triangle points at the Done cell; its
    page's strip, which ends at Launch (AC83), has none, since the sentence says "Done". A v2.5
    project: the tile's and the page's sprint drawings point at the open sprint, and have none with
    no sprint open.
  - **Removed:** the ▲ on an opened phase that meant "read from the bottom up" (frame 6, AC83's "a
    thin line with an arrow pointing up", notes 12 and 19). The thin line stays, and the section
    head's "↑ start at the foot" says the reading order once, so no triangle means two things.
  - A test marked `ac-test: S-001/AC92` renders the five drawings from the fixtures and made-up
    cases (labelled NOT real): a first run, a second run, a gate waiting, a Done project, a v2.5
    project with and without an open sprint, a project not yet read and one that can't be read; and
    checks: exactly one triangle on each drawing that has a present, beside the element its words
    name (the now cell, the Now line, the next-to-reach row), pointing the way given above, at its
    size, in `--ink` in both themes, `aria-hidden`, with no animation or transition; none where there
    is no present; none on a gate row; and no ▲ or other up-pointing triangle on any screen. The
    stage's pull request carries Chromium captures of each drawing at 360 × 740 and 414 × 896, light
    and dark.

- AC93 [trace: V4 → AC93] — When a status mark says that something finished and was confirmed, or
  that something failed, then that mark, and only the mark, is green (`--ok`) or red (`--bad`); words,
  rows, fills and borders take neither; vermilion still means only what needs the owner, gold only
  next to reach, and no third colour joins them.
  - The ruling: P-001-glance2-palette.md, line 1 (quoted in the amendment), with "--bad keeps its
    current values" (its "Read as"). The owner's ask: "I'm not against slight color … I am willing
    to adjust that, for a limited palette that enforces consistent indication of things that are
    going well, and things that aren't."
  - **The tokens, unchanged** (AC81): `--ok` #12733a light, #4cc06a dark; `--bad` #b3162a light,
    #ff6b78 dark. The nine meaningful colours keep their distances (lowest 13.3 light, `--you` and
    `--bad`; 12.2 dark, `--gold` and Build), since no value changes.
  - **Green, on the ✓ only** (the audit, item 1): the ✓ of a reached milestone and of a finished
    phase, on the Timeline, a project page's strip, an opened phase's rows, a Home tile's drawing and
    Plan's Reached list; the ✓ of a sprint's marks merged, review, checks and source-checked (AC60),
    each ✓ in its own span in `--ok`, its word staying `--ink2`; the Done lane's ✓, as built; and a
    "CI … passing" line, which gains a ✓ before its words where it has none.
  - **Red, on the ✕ only:** the ✕ of a milestone not reached ("Design-6 · not reached"); the ✕ of a
    sprint's mark for a review failed, checks failed or a source check failed (AC60), its word staying
    `--ink2`; the ✕ of a project the desk can't read, as built; the ✕ of the failed-load page (AC89
    (h)); a "CI … failing" line, which gains a ✕ before its words, such as a sheet's "What was
    checked: CI on main's head: failing"; and the mismatch mark of a waiting deploy that matches no
    passed pull request (AC72).
  - **Stays ink or grey:** planned, in progress (the half circle), not recorded, no record in the
    model, skipped and not needed; a reached mark in a run later gone back over (the lighter check,
    notes-2 note 2); every absence ("Nothing waiting", "Nothing needs you" and its tick, "checked …
    ago"); the agents' gaps and their grey diamond (AC69); "new"; the stall line, in ink with its
    clock (round 1, item 1); the settle and undo lines, a clock or lock in ink; the Technical, Context
    and Why labels; and every milestone heading ("Bold headings, no colour", P-001-trial-view-notes-1.md,
    stands: only the icon changes).
  - **The rules that keep it limited** (the audit's seven): colour only on a status mark, a ✓ or ✕
    or a status icon at 14 to 16 px, never on a fill, border, row ground or heading; every coloured
    mark keeps its shape and word; green only for a recorded, finished fact (reached, merged, passed,
    confirmed), never for an absence or for quiet; red only for a recorded failure or a failed read,
    never for an agents' gap or for something waiting; where a mark is the owner's and failing (a
    kicked-back card) vermilion wins; gold stays next to reach; no third colour.
  - **The can't-read line's words stay red, as built** (C): round 1's item 2 drew them in `--bad`,
    and the audit's rule 1 keeps them ("Words stay ink or grey, except the can't-read line"). The
    ruling's "never on words" is read as ruling out new red words, not that line.
  - **Gone:** the red border on a Home tile whose project can't be read (`.v2-tile.bad`; the audit's
    F4). The tile's corner, "✕ Can't read since HH:MM", carries it.
  - **Contrast** (the audit, measured): `--ok` 5.26:1 at its lowest (light, on `--chip`), `--bad`
    5.77:1 at its lowest (dark, on `--chip`), so each mark passes WCAG 1.4.11's 3:1 and 1.4.3's 4.5:1
    on every ground it sits on, in both themes.
  - **What this changes** (each by the owner's ruling, as the audit listed them): notes-2 note 23's
    "not by colour" for these marks (the icon in a plain circle stays, and the colour goes with its
    shape); note 28's pick for the tile's checks; AC48's "Milestones are neutral" for the marks only;
    P-001-timeline-labels.md's "colour is left for what needs the owner", which now also allows pass
    and fail on the marks; AC59's, AC60's and AC84's icons; and frames 5, 6, 7b and H5 as drawn.
    P-001-redesign-type.md's one vermilion accent and AC69 are unchanged.
  - A test marked `ac-test: S-001/AC93` renders every trial-view screen from each fixture and
    made-up cases (labelled NOT real: a failed review, failed checks, a failed source check, a CI
    failing line, a deploy mismatch, a milestone not reached, a reached mark in a run gone back over,
    a kicked-back card) in light and dark, and checks, through AC88's cascade: every element whose
    `color` resolves to `--ok` is a ✓ mark in the list above, and every one resolving to `--bad` a ✕
    mark in the list or the can't-read line; no `background`, `border-color` or `outline-color`
    resolves to either; the words beside each mark stay `--ink2` or `--ink`; each case listed under
    "Stays ink or grey" resolves to neither; a kicked-back card's mark stays vermilion; no tile has a
    `--bad` border; and the nine colours' distances and each mark's contrast on its ground as above.

- AC94 [trace: V4 → AC94] — When the owner opens a project's page or its Timeline, then each phase
  leads with all its milestones counted, the project's own and the standard ones it tracks, reached
  of total, with its sprints counted beside them; the standard ones it doesn't use are said in
  words, never as "0 of 5"; and each milestone counts its sprints and how many have merged.
  - The ruling: P-001-glance2-counts.md, line 1. The option as put: "Milestone and sprint counts as
    proposed; pieces counted done-of-total from a task list in each sprint's pull request (an
    operating-model change, then the desk reads it)." The owner's words: "when I look at the
    milestones page I am consistently met with a 0 out of X milestones. Even on phases we've fully
    completed. My understanding is that is referring to the standard milestones. I want to expand
    that to all milestones, in some way that highlights the fact we didn't use the x standard ones
    but we still have y number of milestones and this is what we've completed so far. I want that
    same logic applied to sprints and actions. So I can see the volume progress for each." The
    pieces of work are AC96's.
  - **What is counted, for each phase** (C where marked):
    - **your milestones:** each of the project's own milestones that docs/PROJECT.md section 3 puts in
      the phase, across all its runs, counted once however many runs it appears in, a dropped one
      (AC24's "Dropped") left out;
    - **the standard ones tracked:** each of the phase's standard milestones that has a recorded
      state in the model's trace (reached, not reached or any other recorded state, J11) or that a
      plan line marks "taken on" (AC61), counted once;
    - **the standard ones not tracked:** the phase's others, "not recorded yet" or "no record in the
      model" (AC83's three states), and, apart from them, those a plan line marks "skipped";
    - **T** is your milestones plus the standard ones tracked; **R** those of them reached (an own
      milestone whose plan line carries ` · reached: <date>`, J11; a standard one recorded reached);
    - **the phase's sprints:** every sprint AC60 places in the phase's runs, under a milestone or
      under "Not tied to a milestone", counted once even when it feeds two milestones (PR #44 under
      M2 and M2B) (C); never one AC60 keeps off the Timeline (the asks-merge job's merges, the
      estimate pull requests). Each is merged, not merged or not read, by AC60's merged mark: "✓
      merged" is merged; a sprint J12 does not hold, or whose read failed ("not available", "not
      recorded in what the desk reads"), is not read.
  - **The section head** (AC83): "Milestones by phase · <R> of <T> reached", R and T summed over the
    phases, in place of "yours and the model's <n>"; "↑ start at the foot" stays at its right.
  - **Each phase's folded line** (AC83's one line per phase, still read from the bottom up, its state
    word at the right and its fold mark as built), its detail now two lines:
    - **line 1:** "<R> of <T> reached · <the sprints part>", the sprints part one of "<m> of <s>
      sprints merged" (every sprint's merge known), "<s> sprints: <m> merged, <k> not read" (some not
      read), "<s> sprints, merges not read" (none read), or "no sprints filed yet"; "1 sprint" in the
      singular. With T of 0: "No milestones tracked yet · <the sprints part>" (C). For example (the
      audit's `mix` fixture): "3 of 5 reached · 4 sprints, merges not read";
    - **line 2:** "Standard checklist: <k> tracked · <u> not tracked", or "Standard checklist: none
      tracked (<n>)" when k is 0, adding " · <j> skipped" where plan lines say skipped; n is the
      phase's standard count (24 in all today: Discovery 8, Design 6, Build 5, Launch 5), and k + u +
      j = n. These are words: no "<x> of <n>" is ever given for the checklist alone;
    - AC83's old detail line ("Yours: <ids> · Standard: <k> of <n> <reached | recorded>", with its
      "run <k>: … reached") goes: each id is one tap away in the opened phase (AC95).
  - **Each milestone:**
    - **on the Timeline** (AC84): its fold reads "<n> sprints · <m> merged ▸", or "· <m> merged, <k>
      not read" when some are not read, "· merges not read" when none is, in place of "<n> sprints
      ▸"; a milestone with none keeps its words as built;
    - **in an opened phase** (AC83): an own milestone with work filed reads "work filed · <m> of <n>
      sprints merged" ("work filed · 1 of 1 sprint merged"), the merge part as on the Timeline where
      some are not read; its other state words are unchanged.
  - **The audit's F1 and F2 are fixed by these definitions:** a standard milestone with a recorded
    state in a later run ("Launch-3 · not reached" in run 3) is tracked, so its phase never reads
    "not recorded yet" for it; and an own milestone planned in an earlier run (M3C in run 2) is among
    the phase's milestones.
  - **A v2.5 project:** no phases or milestones; its page and Timeline are unchanged.
  - **Unread records:** a project the desk can't read keeps AC89 (h)'s "Phases: not available", with
    no counts; a count is never given from a partial read.
  - AC90 still applies: a reason shared by two or more rows of a phase is said once at its head.
  - A test marked `ac-test: S-001/AC94` renders the page and the Timeline from `service-desk/`, the
    audit's `text` and `mix` cases (made up, labelled NOT real) and made-up cases: a phase with all
    its sprints merged, some not read, none read and none filed; a sprint feeding two milestones; an
    untied sprint; an asks-merge job's merge; a dropped own milestone; a standard milestone taken on,
    one skipped and one with a recorded state in a later run (F1); an own milestone planned in an
    earlier run (F2); T of 0; and a project that can't be read. It checks the head's sum, each line 1
    and line 2 form and its singular, k + u + j = n, no "<x> of <n>" for the checklist, the Timeline
    fold's and the opened row's sprint words, and that AC83's old detail line is gone.

- AC95 [trace: V4 → AC95] — When the owner opens a phase on a project's page, or reads its Timeline,
  then the project's own milestones and the model's standard checklist sit under their own clear
  heads, the checklist below a rule, its untracked milestones folded into one "not tracked" line a
  tap opens, and the owner's rows weightier than the checklist's.
  - The ruling: P-001-glance2-standard.md, line 1. The option as put: "As proposed; the folded line
    says "6 not tracked this run"." The owner's words: "please visual segregate the standard
    milestones a little bit more than they currently are. The lighter color just kind of gets
    skipped by me and I get confused on what's in or out". P-001-standard-milestones.md (every
    standard milestone shown, skipped ones named) and P-001-redesign-conflicts.md item 2 stand.
  - **In an opened phase** (AC83; the audit, item 5), for each run, the latest first and each earlier
    run alike (earlier runs gain the heads they lack today):
    - **the heads:** "Your milestones · <n>", n the own milestones in that run's list, then
      "Standard checklist · <n> · <k> tracked", or "Standard checklist · <n> · none tracked this
      run", each in `--t-label` (500 11 px) in `--ink`, in place of today's "Yours" and "The model's
      standard <n>" in 400 11 px `--ink2`;
    - **the rule:** a 1 px line in `--line` above the standard head, with an 8 px gap above it;
    - **the rows:** an own milestone's name in the row role, `--t-row` (500 13 px); a standard one's in
      400 13 px, its colour as built; each keeps AC83's icon and state words, the first at the foot;
    - **the standard rows tracked** (AC94's sense) and those a plan line marks skipped are listed,

    outlined box isn't ONLY for the single most important thing on the page. It should be for the

    one thing omits other elements that might be close to or as important." The option as put: "The
    project page gets the boxed sentence and tally; the rule holds desk-wide; the why-not-written box
    becomes a plain line." The owner's round-2 ask: "the occasional usage of outlined boxes or subtle
    callouts that an assist as visual anchors on pages for the most important information on it".

    radius 12 px, padding 12 px, a 6 px gap between its lines, text in `--ink` in the roles the
    lines already have. No edge of any kind: no border, no outline, no edge in `--line`, `--line2`

    `--line2` edge is the text box's look). Its ground is never vermilion. A mark inside it keeps

  - **What may sit in one** (the widened rule): the set of a screen's most important things, such as

- **J25 — A sprint's task list and its steps → the counts (page side; added 2026-11-03, AC94, AC96,
  after the glance audit's round 2).** v3 projects only. No new request: both sources are answers
  the page already holds, so A3's sum (9,952) and J12's query text are unchanged.
  - **Steps of a pipeline-item sprint** (AC96 (a), from stage 1): from the v3 dispatch log J9 reads
    (`dispatch-log/<YYYY-MM>.jsonl`, every month file the page holds), each entry with `"action":
    "dispatch"` (a session starts, J9's shape) whose `item` equals the sprint's id (`Q-013`, a `P-`
    or `E-` item) is one step. An entry that doesn't have J9's shape is skipped, as J9 skips it
    (AC31). The count is of steps the page holds: a month file it can't read makes the count "steps
    not read" (C).
  - **Pieces of work of a pull-request sprint** (AC96 (b), from stage 6): from the pull request's
    `body`, which J12 already fetches. **The form is provisional** (C) until the model change freezes
    its own; before stage 6 opens, a revision of this join replaces this paragraph with the model's
    frozen form and its version, as J10 adopted model S-020's:
    - the section headed by a line exactly `## Tasks`, up to the next line starting `## ` or the
      body's end; a body with none has no task list;
    - in it, each line whose text after any spaces starts `- [ ] `, `- [x] ` or `- [X] ` (or the same
      with `*` in place of `-`) is one piece, at any depth of indent; `[x]` or `[X]` is done. Lines
      inside a fenced code block (between two lines starting with three backticks) are not counted;
    - so each pull request gives `tasks`: `{ "done": <d>, "total": <t> }`, or `null` for no `## Tasks`
      section. A section with no task lines gives `{ "done": 0, "total": 0 }`, which AC96 says as
      "lists no pieces".
  - **Steps of a pull-request sprint** (AC96 (b)): from the field the model change adds to each step's
    record to name its sprint (a dispatch-log entry's, and a Chief of Staff session line's, J13). Its
    name and form are the model's; the revision above names them. Until then none is read.
  - **Which model applies** (C): the forms apply to a project from the model version that adopts
    them, read from its `governance/OPERATING_MODEL_VERSION` (J23's version reads). A project at a
    lower version shows AC96's "no record for this in the model yet"; at that version or later, a pull
    request with no `## Tasks` section reads "lists no pieces", one merged before the project adopted
    the form included (a known gap, C: the desk reads no adoption date, and the words state a fact,
    not a fault).
  - **What the page keeps** (J12, changed): each kept pull request gains `tasks` as above, the two
    counts only, never a task's text. The key moves from `desk-pulls-v3` to `desk-pulls-v4`;
    `desk-pulls-v3` is removed on load and every entry read again from J12, as each earlier move did;
    an entry lacking `tasks` reads "pieces not read" until J12 reads it again.
  - **Awkward cases:**
    - **a box ticked after the merge:** shown from the next head change only if the pull request is
      among the newest 100, J12's known gap for a body edited after its merge;
    - **more than 300 pull requests:** a sprint among the older ones reads "pieces not read" (J12's
      awkward case);
    - **J12's read fails or is rate-limited:** every pull-request sprint reads "pieces not read", its
      reason one tap away (AC41); the project is never "Can't read" for it;
    - **a task line quoted inside a `>` block:** counted, since it sits in the section (C);
    - **two `## Tasks` sections:** the first only (C);
    - **a sprint listed under two milestones:** its pieces count once in its phase (AC94's rule for
      sprints) and once under each milestone.
  - A test marked `join-test: S-001/J25` covers it with made-up dispatch logs and pull-request bodies
    (labelled NOT real in tests/desk/fixtures/README.md): steps by `item`, a malformed entry skipped,
    an unread month; each task-line form, upper and lower `x`, `*` bullets, an indented one, one in a
    code fence, a quoted one, no section, an empty section and two sections; the kept entry holding
    the two counts and no text; `desk-pulls-v3` removed and re-read; a version below and at the
    adopting one; and the request count per J12 read unchanged.
